newsitem.title: UK: Wace warns on trading profits, small yr loss.
newsitem.headline: Wace warns on trading profits, small yr loss.

text.p: Imaging and printing company Wace Group Plc said a continuing lack of consistent growth in sales meant that trading profits for 1996 would be "substantially lower than current market expectations."

In a statement, the company said that exceptional charges of 3.95 million stg in the first half and of approximately 9.0 million stg in the second half, along with difficult trading conditions, made it anticipate "a small loss for the year."

The company said it had undertaken a strategic review and as a result it had exchanged contracts for the sale of its publication pre-press business for a nominal consideration to concentrate on its electronic publishing services.
It said it had closed its Glasgow site and was streamlining other sites because the UK commercial print market remained "highly competitive."

Wace said it had accelerated plans to reorganise its Paris business while Wace USA had decided to form strategic alliances with major printing groups instead of buying and developing its own business.
As a result, it said, the print businesses in Grand Rapids and Memphis would be sold and a small print operation in New York would be closed.

All of its U.S. operations would be concentrated on image management processes, the company said, with five sites in Chicago streamlined into one new location in the suburbs which will "produce considerable efficiency gains."
It said it was also selling a printer in Holland which it acquired in December 1995 as part of the purchase of Ferry Pickering but which had no strategic importance.
Wace said its development would be focused on digital imaging in the growth areas of electronic publishing, on-line digital media and multi-product printing and packaging.
"The board has taken decisive steps to extract the group from loss-making commodity markets where it is clear there are now no signs of a prompt recovery," it said.
